title: Space Mart: A post-collapse cyberpunk game (prototype)
author: Key_Programmer_5793
selftext:
I started this game as a side quest, mostly to refresh my aging web dev skills...but now it's quickly growing into a post-collapse cyberpunk text-adventure game (in-browser/html5).

You start out by talking to the clerk, and you can access different areas of the store by asking questions. One specific request gets you into the text adventure, and I just completed the first chapter, with the potential to have hundreds(?) of doors that each lead into their own adventures.

My next step is to add player inventory, a vending machine with survival items, and write stories for each door that will present new items and storylines to use said items. After that maybe a crafting bench to combine items.

If this sounds at all interesting to you, and you have 10min to mess around with this initial build/prototype, please check out Space Mart and lemme know what you think/find.  
  
Thanks for looking!

Website: [SpaceMart.Store](http://SpaceMart.Store)

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: Looks like you only keep the last 8 messages in history, kind of puts a real damper on any sort of interesting long running conversation.

replies.author: Key_Programmer_5793
replies.body: Great suggestion! I was just thinking theplayer would ask for specific areas to go, but letting the clerkim roll as a chatbot with memory is a great idea - i could place additional lore in there, a FAQ of the game/site mechanics, etc. Great suggestion, thank you very much!

replies.author: Key_Programmer_5793
replies.body:
I just upped the memory to 15 questions before he could potentially repeat an answer, and the maximum questions you can ask per day is 69. Also gave him a little more temperature/variation in answering for richer prompts, and his ability to lean into lore, mechanics, etc.   
  
Again, thank you for pointing that out u/Aromatic-Low-4578, I probably wouldn't have considered it otherwise.
